check_contrast.description: Compute the WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio between a text color and a background, with pass or fail flags for AA and AAA at normal and large text sizes and for graphics. The step to run before a color pair ships, with one boolean to branch on. No API key required.
check_contrast.name: check_contrast

parameters.description: The color of the text, icon or foreground. Any CSS color works: a hex code such as #7c5cff (bare digits are fine, the # is added), rgb(), hsl(), oklch(), or a named color such as tomato. Any transparency is dropped.
parameters.name: foreground

parameters.description: The color behind it. Any CSS color works: a hex code such as #7c5cff (bare digits are fine, the # is added), rgb(), hsl(), oklch(), or a named color such as tomato. Any transparency is dropped.
parameters.name: background

check_contrast.result_str_template: {colorui_check_contrast,foreground} on {colorui_check_contrast,background} has a contrast ratio of {colorui_check_contrast,ratio}:1, grade {colorui_check_contrast,grade}.

aa.description: Whether the pair meets WCAG 2.1 level AA.

graphics.description: True when icons and interface parts pass AA (a ratio of 3 or more).

large_text.description: True when large text passes AA (a ratio of 3 or more). Large means 18pt, or 14pt bold, and up.

normal_text.description: True when body text passes AA (a ratio of 4.5 or more).

aaa.description: Whether the pair meets WCAG 2.1 level AAA.

large_text.description: True when large text passes AAA (a ratio of 4.5 or more).

normal_text.description: True when body text passes AAA (a ratio of 7 or more).

background.description: The background color that was checked, as the service echoed it.

foreground.description: The text color that was checked, as the service echoed it.

grade.description: The best level the pair reaches, as the service grades it: AAA, AA, AA Large (only large text passes), or Fail.

passes_aa.description: True when body text passes AA. This is the field to branch on before shipping a text and background pair.

passes_aaa.description: True when body text passes AAA, the stricter level.

ratio.description: The WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio, from 1 (no contrast) to 21 (black on white), to two decimals.

check_service_status.description: Check whether ColorUI is answering, how quickly, and how much of the rate limit is left this minute. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can branch on it, pace itself, or fall back to a saved palette when the service is down. Being throttled is reported separately from being down. No API key required.

mock_response.message: ColorUI is up and converting colors, with 59 of 60 requests left in this minute.

check_service_status.name: check_service_status

message.description: What happened, in a sentence worth posting.

online.description: True when the service answered with a converted color. This is the field to branch on.

rate_limit_resets_at.description: When the current minute's budget refills, as a UTC time like 2026-09-11T14:05:00Z, or null when the service did not say.

rate_limited.description: True when the answer was a throttle (HTTP 429). Being throttled is not the same as being down.

reachable.description: True when something answered at all, even with an error. False means the request never landed.

requests_remaining.description: How many requests are left in the current minute, out of 60 per IP address, or null when the service did not say. A workflow can wait when this runs low.

response_time_ms.description: How long the request took, in milliseconds, or null when nothing came back.

status_code.description: The HTTP status that came back, or null when nothing did.

convert_color.description: Convert any CSS color into HEX, RGB, HSL, LCH, OKLCH and LAB, all at once or one at a time, each with its components and a CSS string ready to paste. All at once also gives HSV, the color's luminance and whether it is light or dark. The step that turns a designer's oklch() into the rgb() a legacy tool needs, or a named color into its hex for a template. No API key required.
convert_color.name: convert_color

parameters.description: The color to convert. Any CSS color works: a hex code such as #7c5cff (bare digits are fine, the # is added), rgb(), hsl(), oklch(), or a named color such as tomato. Any transparency is dropped.
parameters.name: color

parameters.description: Optional. Which format to convert into. Every format at once by default, which is the choice for a step that will need more than one.
parameters.name: format

css.description: The one string to paste: the CSS of the format asked for, or the hex when every format was.

format.description: The format that was asked for: all, hex, rgb, hsl, lch, oklch or lab.

hex.description: The color as lowercase hex, e.g. #7c5cff. Null when a different single format was asked for.

hsl.description: The color in HSL, with its components and a CSS string. Null when this format was not asked for.

css.description: The color as a CSS hsl() string ready to paste into a stylesheet, as the service writes it, e.g. hsl(251.8, 100%, 68%).

l.description: Lightness, as a percentage from 0 to 100.

s.description: Saturation, as a percentage from 0 to 100.

hsv.description: The color in HSV (hue, saturation and value), the model most color pickers use. CSS has no hsv(), so it comes as numbers alone. Null unless every format was asked for.

s.description: Saturation, as a percentage from 0 to 100.

v.description: Value (brightness), as a percentage from 0 to 100.

input.description: The color as it was given, echoed back by the service.

is_light.description: True when ColorUI counts the color as light, so dark text reads best on it; false when it is dark. Null unless every format was asked for.

lab.description: The color in LAB, with its components and a CSS string. Null when this format was not asked for.

a.description: The green to red axis; negative is green, positive is red.

b.description: The blue to yellow axis; negative is blue, positive is yellow.

css.description: The color as a CSS lab() string ready to paste into a stylesheet, as the service writes it, e.g. lab(49.76% 44.54 -78.38).

lch.description: The color in LCH, with its components and a CSS string. Null when this format was not asked for.

css.description: The color as a CSS lch() string ready to paste into a stylesheet, as the service writes it, e.g. lch(49.76% 90.15 299.61).

luminance.description: The color's relative luminance, from 0 (black) to 1 (white): the figure WCAG contrast is worked out from. Null unless every format was asked for.

oklch.description: The color in OKLCH, with its components and a CSS string. Null when this format was not asked for.

css.description: The color as a CSS oklch() string ready to paste into a stylesheet, as the service writes it, e.g. oklch(59.9% 0.2299 286.2).

rgb.description: The color in RGB, with its components and a CSS string. Null when this format was not asked for.

css.description: The color as a CSS rgb() string ready to paste into a stylesheet, as the service writes it, e.g. rgb(124, 92, 255).

generate_harmony_palette.description: Build a palette around one color by a color-wheel rule: complementary, analogous, triadic, tetradic, split-complementary, square or monochromatic. The step that turns a brand color into a set of accents that sit well with it, as hex codes with a link to the palette. No API key required.
generate_harmony_palette.name: generate_harmony_palette

parameters.description: The color to build the palette around. Any CSS color works: a hex code such as #7c5cff (bare digits are fine, the # is added), rgb(), hsl(), oklch(), or a named color such as tomato. Any transparency is dropped.
parameters.name: base

parameters.description: The color-wheel rule that picks the other colors from the base: complementary for its opposite, analogous for its neighbours, triadic or square for evenly spaced accents, monochromatic for shades of the base itself.
parameters.name: harmony

generate_harmony_palette.result_str_template: Generated a {colorui_generate_harmony_palette,harmony} palette of {colorui_generate_harmony_palette,count} colors around {colorui_generate_harmony_palette,base}: {colorui_generate_harmony_palette,share_url}

base.description: The color the palette was built around.

colors.description: The palette, as lowercase hex codes in the service's order, e.g. #7c5cff.

count.description: How many colors are in the palette.

harmony.description: The harmony rule the palette follows.

share_url.description: A link that opens the palette on colorui.io, e.g. https://colorui.io/p/0b0b1a7c5cffff2bd606f5fffbbf24. Null when the service gave none.

source.description: How the palette was made, as the service reports it: ai for a prompt, harmony for a rule, random for a draw.

generate_palette_from_prompt.description: Generate a five-color palette from a few words about what it is for, such as a brand, a product or a mood. Comes back as hex codes with the intent the service read into the prompt, the role each color plays (background, surface, primary, accent, support) with why, and a link to the palette on colorui.io. The same prompt and variant always give the same palette. No API key required.
generate_palette_from_prompt.display_name: Generate a palette from a prompt

intent.label: Gaming / Esports
intent.rationale: High-chroma neon cyan, magenta and violet against deep backgrounds nail the gaming aesthetic.

narratives.text: Accent role: this bright yellow pulls the eye to the most important moment.
Background role: this bright magenta sets the canvas mood.
Support role: this bright magenta fills the supporting roles - secondary buttons, badges.
Primary role: this mid-tone yellow carries the brand and primary actions.
Surface role: this bright teal lifts cards and panels off the background.

generate_palette_from_prompt.name: generate_palette_from_prompt

parameters.description: What the palette is for, in a few words: a brand, a mood, a product. The service reads the intent and designs a palette to suit it.
parameters.name: prompt

parameters.description: Optional. A number from 0 to 99 that picks one of the palettes the prompt could give; left empty, the service uses 0. The same prompt and variant always return the same palette, so change it to get a different take on the same brief.
parameters.name: variant

colors.description: The palette, as lowercase hex codes in the service's order, e.g. #7c5cff.

count.description: How many colors are in the palette.

intent.description: What the service took the prompt to be asking for. Null when it gave no reading.

key.description: The intent's short identifier, e.g. gaming.

label.description: The intent as a label, e.g. Gaming / Esports.

rationale.description: Why the service read the prompt that way.

narratives.description: One explanation per color, in palette order. Empty when the service gave none.

items.description: Why one color of the palette is there.

color.description: The color the explanation is about, as hex.

family.description: Its hue family, e.g. violet or teal.

role.description: The part it plays in an interface: background, surface, primary, accent or support.

summary.description: The color in a line, e.g. Bright violet - futuristic and bold.

temperature.description: Whether it reads as warm or cool.

text.description: Why it suits its role, in a sentence.

weight.description: How light or deep it is, in ColorUI's words: pale, bright, mid-tone, deep or near-black.

prompt.description: The brief the palette was designed for.

roles.description: The palette's color for each role, as hex, so a step can take the primary color straight from roles.primary. A role the palette doesn't fill is null.

accent.description: The color that draws the eye to what matters most.

background.description: The color that sets the canvas.

primary.description: The brand color, for primary actions.

support.description: The color for secondary buttons, badges and the like.

surface.description: The color for cards and panels.

share_url.description: A link that opens the palette on colorui.io, e.g. https://colorui.io/p/0b0b1a7c5cffff2bd606f5fffbbf24. Null when the service gave none.

source.description: How the palette was made, as the service reports it: ai for a prompt, harmony for a rule, random for a draw.

variant.description: The variant that was used, 0 to 99; 0 when none was given. The same prompt and variant always give the same palette.

generate_random_palette.description: Draw a palette of two to eight colors at random, as hex codes with a link to the palette on colorui.io. The step for a fresh scheme every run: a color of the day, a placeholder theme, or inspiration to pass on to a designer. No API key required.
generate_random_palette.name: generate_random_palette

parameters.description: Optional. How many colors to draw, between 2 and 8. 5 by default.
parameters.name: count

generate_random_palette.result_str_template: Generated a random palette of {colorui_generate_random_palette,count} colors: {colorui_generate_random_palette,share_url}

colors.description: The palette, as lowercase hex codes in the service's order, e.g. #7c5cff.

count.description: How many colors are in the palette.

share_url.description: A link that opens the palette on colorui.io, e.g. https://colorui.io/p/0b0b1a7c5cffff2bd606f5fffbbf24. Null when the service gave none.

source.description: How the palette was made, as the service reports it: ai for a prompt, harmony for a rule, random for a draw.

description: Color tools from ColorUI's free public API: convert any CSS color into HEX, RGB, HSL, LCH, OKLCH and LAB at once, check the WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio between a text color and a background with AA and AAA pass or fail flags, and generate palettes from a few words about a brand or a mood, from a harmony rule around a base color, or at random. Every palette comes back as hex codes with a link to it on colorui.io, so a workflow can turn a brief into swatches, check a color pair before it ships, or convert a designer's OKLCH into the RGB a legacy tool needs. No account or API key required.
